digest.lead: The big story today is Simon Willison's analysis that Anthropic and OpenAI have reached product-market fit, sparking major discussion on Hacker News with 835 points and nearly 1,000 comments.
digest.summary: Meanwhile, Claude Code shipped incremental improvements with better Git LFS handling and terminal sizing, while tensions between AI leaders continue over jobs impact messaging.

stories.headline: Industry Observer Declares Anthropic Has Achieved Product-Market Fit
stories.summary: Simon Willison published an analysis arguing that both Anthropic and OpenAI have found genuine product-market fit [1]. The post generated significant discussion on Hacker News, attracting 835 points and 963 comments [1].
stories.impact: This validates Anthropic's strategic positioning and suggests Claude has moved beyond early adoption into mainstream utility for knowledge workers and developers.

sources.title: I think Anthropic and OpenAI have found product-market fit

stories.headline: Anthropic and OpenAI Clash Over AI Jobs Impact Messaging
stories.summary: The two leading AI companies are taking opposing stances on how to communicate about AI's potential impact on employment [1]. The disagreement highlights strategic differences in public positioning around AI safety and economic disruption [1].
stories.impact: This public disagreement could influence regulatory discussions and enterprise adoption decisions as companies weigh AI investment against workforce concerns.

sources.title: OpenAI and Anthropic dig in against each other on AI jobs apocalypse

stories.headline: Claude Code Adds Git LFS Support and Terminal Improvements
stories.summary: Version 2.1.153 introduces a `skipLfs` option for Git operations, better npm update notifications, and enhanced terminal integration [1]. The update also improves autocomplete functionality in agent dispatch and provides better terminal sizing for status line commands [1].
key_points: New `skipLfs` option prevents unnecessary Git LFS downloads during repository operations
Status line commands now receive terminal dimensions for properly sized output
Agent autocomplete now suggests native slash commands and bundled skills
stories.impact: These improvements streamline developer workflows, particularly for teams working with large repositories or custom terminal setups in Claude Code.

stories.headline: Use CLAUDE.md files to provide persistent context for your projects
stories.summary: CLAUDE.md files let you give Claude permanent instructions and context about your project that persist across conversations. Claude automatically loads these files when working in your codebase, eliminating the need to repeatedly explain project structure and conventions.
actionable_steps: Create a CLAUDE.md file in your project root directory
Write clear instructions about your project's structure, conventions, and requirements
Add import statements for additional context files if needed

stories.headline: Set up hooks to automate Claude Code workflows at key events
stories.summary: Hooks allow you to run custom scripts or commands automatically when specific events occur in Claude Code, such as session start, prompt submission, or instruction loading. This enables automated setup, validation, or custom integrations.
actionable_steps: Create hook configuration files in your project's .claude directory
Define hook events (SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, etc.) and their corresponding actions
Configure hook handlers with command, HTTP, or MCP tool fields as needed
Test hooks using the /hooks menu to verify they trigger correctly

stories.headline: Organize project rules using .claude/rules/ directory structure
stories.summary: The .claude/rules/ directory lets you break down complex project instructions into organized, manageable files. This makes it easier to maintain large codebases and share specific rules across multiple projects.
actionable_steps: Create a .claude/rules/ directory in your project root
Split your CLAUDE.md instructions into focused rule files (e.g., coding-style.md, testing.md)
Use symlinks to share common rules across multiple projects
Reference rule files from your main CLAUDE.md using import statements

stories.headline: Enable feedback surveys for enterprise OpenTelemetry users
stories.summary: If your enterprise captures telemetry data through OpenTelemetry, you can now re-enable Claude Code's session quality surveys to gather user feedback. This helps organizations collect structured feedback data alongside their existing telemetry infrastructure.
actionable_steps: Verify that session quality surveys now appear in your Claude Code interface

stories.headline: Use defer permission in PreToolUse hooks to pause headless sessions
stories.summary: You can now pause headless Claude Code sessions at tool calls and resume them later with permission evaluation. This allows for better control over automated workflows that need human approval.
actionable_steps: Set up a PreToolUse hook in your Claude Code configuration
Return 'defer' as the permission decision in the hook
The hook will re-evaluate the tool call upon resumption
